hypothesis_or_reduction_question: Does the RV01-motivated residual-deadzone delay learner retain a stable mechanism-specific advantage over a stronger ordinary scalar adaptive filter when information access, persistent state, and DEV-selected control count are matched?
synthetic_or_dev_inputs_used: Same fixed synthetic RV01 delay world as the preceding probe: latent delays 1/3/5 ms; Gaussian noise sigma 0.55 ms; signed 3 ms outliers; DEV probability 0.06 on seeds 20260901-20260905; disjoint TEST probabilities 0/0.03/0.06/0.12/0.20 on seeds 20260918-20260922.
implementation_or_experiment_performed: Implemented a generic innovation-gated EWMA with one persistent scalar and two DEV-selected controls; fixed comparator family/grids before TEST; independently selected each filter once on DEV; froze parameters; opened the disjoint TEST sweep once; committed deterministic NON_EVIDENTIARY result and tests.
observations: Deadzone won the 0%, 3% and 6% outlier regimes; generic innovation-gated EWMA won 12% and 20%. The crossover moved earlier than with clipped EWMA, demonstrating stronger reduction pressure but not full reduction across the fixed regimes.
what_would_falsify_or_reduce_it: A prospectively fixed stronger generic robust filter family that, under matched information/state/tuning/resource constraints, robustly dominates the RV01-motivated mechanism across all predeclared held-out process/noise regimes would reduce the mechanism-specific story further. Conversely, stable RV01-specific advantage across materially stronger matched controls would be required before formalization is worth reconsidering.
candidate_formal_question: Under prospectively matched information access, persistent state, parameter/training/tuning budget and compute/resource budget, does an RV01-specific learned-delay mechanism provide a stable held-out timing/recovery advantage over strong generic robust adaptive filters across predeclared process/noise regimes?
